steps.do: Find every personal checking account that passes all four checks. (1) Tenure: the referrer's tenure meets the account's minimum (Light Green 14 days; Blue, Green, Green Fee-Free, Light Blue, Gold Years 30; Dark Green, Evergreen, Purple 45; Bluest 60). (2) Deposit: the planned new-money deposit meets the account's qualifying deposit (Light Green $100, Green Fee-Free $300, Blue/Green/Light Blue $500, Evergreen $750, Dark Green/Purple/Gold Years $1,000, Bluest $2,000), and for Bluest also its $75,000 opening deposit. (3) Age: the referred person's age fits (Light Green 13-24, Dark Green 17-26, Gold Years 62+, all others 18+). (4) Cap: this year's referrals of that type are below its annual cap. The account types the referrer holds do not matter. Among the accounts that pass, recommend the one with the highest referrer + referred bonus, and state both amounts.

steps.do: Keep only the business checking programs that pass three checks: the referred deposit meets the required deposit, the referrer's tenure meets the minimum, and the referrer's referrals for that type this calendar year are below its annual cap. Drop Sky Blue unless the business is within 4 years of formation. The account types the referrer already holds do not matter. Recommend the program with the highest referrer bonus.

done_when: The customer is verified and logged, or told they could not be verified. Their referral history and account tenure have been checked from the records. Then one of two outcomes holds. (a) The customer was told the referral cannot be submitted now and why: rolling window full, tenure too short, same registered address, referred party not new or same business owner, signer under 18, or no program's deposit or age rule met. No recommendation was given and nothing was submitted. (b) The customer was told the eligible account to use (personal: highest combined bonus; business: highest referrer bonus), with both bonus amounts, the qualifying deposit and its window, and the conditions. They have submitted submit_referral with that account type ending in 'Account' (or know to do so), and the result has been explained.
